To run GTA 5 with heavy mods and record gameplay using OBS in 2026, you need a laptop that significantly exceeds the game's base recommended requirements. Because GTA 5 is heavily CPU-bound—especially with mods that add traffic, high-quality textures, and complex scripts—and OBS recording adds a secondary load, your priority should be a powerful multi-core processor and a robust GPU.

### Recommended Laptop Specifications for 2026
For a smooth, high-quality experience while recording, aim for these "sweet spot" specifications:

*   **Processor (CPU):** Look for high-performance mobile chips (e.g., **Intel Core i7/i9 14th Gen HX series** or **AMD Ryzen 7/9 7000/8000/9000 series**). GTA 5 relies heavily on single-core performance for game logic and multi-core performance for handling mods and OBS encoding.
*   **Graphics Card (GPU):** An **NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 or RTX 4080 (laptop)** is highly recommended. These cards support DLSS and have dedicated NVENC encoders, which are critical for recording gameplay in OBS without significantly impacting your in-game frame rate.
*   **Memory (RAM):** **32GB DDR5** is the new standard for heavy modding. While 16GB might launch the game, heavy texture packs and background apps (OBS, browser, Discord) will quickly exceed this, causing stuttering.
*   **Storage:** A minimum of **1TB NVMe SSD** (Gen4 or Gen5) is essential. GTA 5 and its mods require fast read speeds to prevent "pop-in" (textures loading slowly).
*   **Display:** If you plan to record, a **1440p (QHD) display** is ideal. It provides enough workspace for OBS overlays while keeping the game looking sharp.

### Why These Specs Matter
*   **CPU-Bound Nature:** GTA 5's engine struggles with dense traffic and complex mods. A "beefy" CPU prevents the frame-time spikes that cause the game to feel "choppy" even if the average FPS seems high.
*   **The "Recording Tax":** OBS uses system resources to encode your video. Using the **NVIDIA NVENC encoder** (available on RTX cards) offloads this work from your CPU to the GPU, which is the most efficient way to record while playing.
*   **Modding Overhead:** Heavy mods often drastically increase VRAM usage. An 8GB VRAM card is a baseline, but 12GB+ is better if you intend to use 4K texture packs or intensive graphical overhaul mods (like ENB or Ray Tracing presets).

### Buying Advice for 2026
*   **Prioritize Cooling:** High-end laptops (like the **Lenovo Legion Pro 7i, ASUS ROG Strix SCAR, or MSI Vector series**) are designed with better thermal management. If a laptop overheats, it will "throttle" (slow down) to protect itself, ruining your recording quality.
*   **Avoid Budget Entry-Level:** While an RTX 4050 or 3050 can "run" the game, they will struggle with heavy mod lists and recording simultaneously. These entry-level cards often lack the VRAM required for high-resolution texture mods.
*   **Future Proofing:** If your budget allows, opting for an RTX 4080 provides a significant performance cushion, allowing you to run modern, demanding titles alongside your heavily modified GTA 5 for years to come.

The search for "GTA 5 laptop Menyoo AddonPeds graphic mods custom ragdolls OBS recording requirements" returned the following summary:
To run GTA 5 with heavy modding (Menyoo, AddonPeds, graphic mods, custom ragdolls) while recording with OBS, you need a system that exceeds the base game requirements significantly. Modding—especially graphic overhauls—and OBS recording are both resource-intensive tasks.

### **Recommended Laptop Specifications**
For a smooth experience at 1080p, look for a modern gaming laptop with these specs:

*   **GPU (Graphics Card):** **NVIDIA RTX 3060 / 4060 or better.** Graphic mods (like ENB or reshades) and high-resolution textures require significant VRAM (at least 6GB, preferably 8GB+).
*   **CPU (Processor):** **Intel Core i5 (12th Gen+) or AMD Ryzen 5 (5000 series+).** Modding adds many scripts and assets that the CPU must process simultaneously with OBS encoding.
*   **RAM:** **16GB minimum; 32GB recommended.** When you add custom peds and high-poly models, your RAM usage will spike. 16GB is the bare minimum for stable multitasking (Game + OBS + Discord/Browser).
*   **Storage:** **512GB+ SSD (NVMe).** GTA 5 and its mods should **always** be installed on an SSD to prevent "pop-in" issues and long loading times.

---

### **Modding & Recording Considerations**

#### **Modding Requirements (Menyoo, AddonPeds, etc.)**
*   **Essential Tools:** You will need the latest versions of **ScriptHookV**, **ASI Loader**, and **OpenIV**.
*   **Single-Player Only:** Always keep your modded game files separate from your clean game files or ensure you are playing in **offline mode** to avoid any risk of bans if you accidentally launch GTA Online.
*   **Performance Impact:** Adding custom ragdoll physics and "AddonPeds" increases the load on your CPU. If you notice stuttering, lower your "Population Density" and "Population Variety" settings in the in-game menu.

#### **OBS Recording Tips**
*   **Hardware Encoding:** In OBS, go to **Settings > Output > Recording** and set the **Video Encoder** to **NVIDIA NVENC H.264**. This uses your graphics card to handle the recording, taking the load off your CPU and preventing frame drops in-game.
*   **Don't Overload:** If your laptop starts to overheat, your performance will drop (thermal throttling). Ensure you are playing on a hard, flat surface or using a laptop cooling pad.
*   **Capture Method:** Use "Game Capture" mode in OBS for the best performance; "Display Capture" is generally less efficient and can cause lower FPS.

### **Summary Checklist**
| Component | Minimum for Mods + OBS | Recommended for Smooth Performance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GPU** | RTX 3050 | RTX 4060 / 4070 |
| **CPU** | Core i5 / Ryzen 5 | Core i7 / Ryzen 7 |
| **RAM** | 16 GB | 32 GB |
| **Storage** | SSD | NVMe SSD |

**Note:** Always back up your game folder (`Grand Theft Auto V`) before installing any mods. This allows you to revert to a "clean" state easily if a mod causes the game to crash or corrupts your files.

Running a heavily modded GTA 5 (especially with script-heavy mods like Menyoo, AddonPeds, and 10+ active custom ragdoll physics) while simultaneously recording via OBS is an intense workload. 

GTA 5 is an older engine, and it is notoriously **CPU-bound**. When you add custom ragdolls and scripts, you hammer the CPU. Add high-resolution graphic mods (like NVE or QuantV), and your GPU and VRAM take a massive hit. On a laptop, this extreme dual-load (Game + OBS) leads directly to heat, which causes **thermal throttling** (the laptop intentionally slowing itself down to prevent melting), resulting in massive lag spikes and crashes.

To avoid this, you must buy a laptop with excellent cooling and the right component balance. Always prioritize an **NVIDIA GPU** because you can use their **NVENC encoder** in OBS, which forces the GPU to handle the video recording, saving your CPU from completely choking.

Here are the exact hardware requirements to pull this off without crashing.

### 1. The Exact MINIMUM Specs
*This is the absolute floor to run these mods and record at 1080p 60fps. Expect some frame drops when multiple ragdolls interact or explosions happen.*
*   **CPU:** Intel Core i5-12500H or AMD Ryzen 5 6600H (You need at least 6 cores/12 threads. Weaker CPUs will freeze the game when physics calculations spike).
*   **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 3060 or RTX 4050 **(6GB VRAM minimum)**. 6GB is the bare minimum so your graphic mods don't cause an "Out of Memory" crash.
*   **RAM:** 16GB DDR4 or DDR5.
*   **Storage:** 1TB NVMe SSD. (Do not get 512GB; a modded GTA 5 install can easily exceed 200GB alone).

### 2. The RECOMMENDED Specs (To Avoid Lag and Crashes)
*This is the "sweet spot" combo for a smooth 1440p/1080p experience where your framerate stays stable even when the screen is full of chaos.*
*   **CPU:** Intel Core i7-13700HX / i7-14700HX or AMD Ryzen 7 7745HX / Ryzen 9 7845HX. (The **"HX"** suffix is crucial here—it means it's a desktop-class processor squeezed into a laptop, offering the multi-core power needed for Menyoo scripts + AddonPeds).
*   **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 4070 (8GB VRAM) or ideally an **RTX 4080 (12GB VRAM)**. High-res AddonPeds and graphic mods eat VRAM for breakfast. The 4080 provides a massive safety net.
*   **RAM:** **32GB DDR5**. 16GB is no longer enough for heavy modding + OBS + Windows background tasks. 32GB prevents the stuttering caused when your system runs out of memory.
*   **Storage:** 1TB or 2TB Gen 4 NVMe SSD. Fast storage stops "texture pop-in" (where buildings load slowly as you drive fast).

---

### 3. Specific Laptop Recommendations for a Beginner (2026)
Since you are fighting thermal throttling, you cannot just buy any laptop with these specs. A thin-and-light laptop will overheat in 10 minutes. You need a "thick" laptop chassis with a robust cooling system (vapor chambers or liquid metal). 

Here are the best beginner-friendly models to look for today:

**The Top Pick (Best Balance of Cooling & Price):**
*   **Lenovo Legion Pro 5i (or Pro 7i)** 
    *   **Spec to buy:** Intel i7-13700HX or 14700HX, RTX 4070, 32GB RAM. 
    *   **Why:** Lenovo's Legion Pro series is famous for having some of the best thermal designs in the industry. It can run at maximum power for hours with minimal throttling. The Lenovo Vantage software makes it very easy for beginners to set the fans to "Performance Mode."

**The Premium Option (Maximum Power & VRAM):**
*   **ASUS ROG Strix G16 or SCAR 16**
    *   **Spec to buy:** Intel i9-14900HX, RTX 4080 (12GB), 32GB RAM.
    *   **Why:** ASUS applies liquid metal to the CPU/GPU straight from the factory, which drastically lowers temperatures. The RTX 4080 with 12GB of VRAM will handle any graphic mod (like NVE) you throw at it without crashing.

**The Budget-Conscious Pick:**
*   **Acer Predator Helios 16**
    *   **Spec to buy:** Intel i7, RTX 4060 or 4070, 16GB RAM (upgradeable to 32GB later).
    *   **Why:** Offers great cooling fans and high power limits for the GPU, giving you near-desktop performance for a bit less money than the Legion or ROG.

### 4. Crucial Tips for Your Setup
1.  **Use NVENC in OBS:** When you set up OBS, go to Output settings and ensure your Encoder is set to **NVIDIA NVENC H.264** or **HEVC**. If you leave it on x264 (CPU encoding), your game *will* stutter and crash.
2.  **Elevate the Laptop:** Never play flat on a desk. Buy a cheap laptop stand to lift the back up by 2 inches so the intake fans can breathe. For heavy modding, a forced-air cooling pad (like the *IETS GT500* or *GT600*) will drop your temperatures by 10-15°C and completely prevent thermal throttling.
3.  **Lower Population Density:** In GTA 5's graphics settings, turn down "Population Density" and "Population Variety." You are adding 10+ custom ragdolls; you need to remove the random AI citizens to free up CPU cycles so the game engine doesn't choke.
